title: In Chinese Calligraphy, You Can't Fix a Single Stroke | China Travel Expert
description:
In Chinese calligraphy, there is no eraser and no undo — the ink hits the paper once, and whatever you wrote is what stays.

That's what makes 书法 so hard: the brush, ink, paper and inkstone (the "Four Treasures of the Study", 文房四宝) leave a permanent mark, so every stroke has to land in the right order and the right direction, in one confident motion. Get it wrong and you don't correct it — you start the whole sheet again. For thousands of years the result has been read not just as writing but as a portrait of the writer's discipline and character.

🧭 Expert Tip: In any old town, look for a shop selling the "Four Treasures" — a wolf- or goat-hair brush, an ink stick, rice paper and an inkstone — and ask to try a stroke before you buy.

一笔落纸，永不能改——这就是中国书法。
